matchups.recap: Rob got absolutely eviscerated 120.1 to 91.9, and frankly, getting boat-raced by 28 points is the kind of ass-kicking that makes you question every decision you made on draft day. Whatever dumpster fire of a roster you assembled this week clearly decided it had better things to do than actually score points—maybe your players were all too busy texting their agents about getting traded to literally anywhere else. Flamur showed up with a functioning football team while you showed up with a participation trophy and a prayer, and we all know how that turned out.

Rinor got absolutely skull-fucked by 4.1 points—so close you could taste it, yet still couldn't close the deal. His team managed to put up 99.9 like some kind of participation trophy, while Arben waltzed to victory with a score that actually respects the concept of winning. This is what happens when you draft like you're picking players out of a hat at a gas station—you end up watching wins slip through your fingers like wet shit. Better luck next week, champ, because this one's gonna sting like a motherfucker.

Adam got absolutely dicked down by 12.7 points this week—which, considering how thin his roster is, might actually be the most action he's seen all season. He's out here looking like he drafted with his eyes closed and his hands tied behind his back, while Nori's squad showed up ready to play actual football. Adam's team didn't just lose, it got fucking embarrassed, and at this point he should probably check if his players are actually alive or just weekend cameos between their real jobs. Better luck next week, champ—though based on that lineup, "better" might be a generous fucking word.

Rilind got absolutely cock-blocked by 5.9 points this week—so close he could taste it, but not quite close enough to stop Ben from taking his lunch money. You had all the opportunity in the world and still managed to leave points on the bench like some kind of lineup management amateur. Next time maybe don't bench your studs in a must-win week and pray for garbage time heroics. That's not a strategy, that's just the sound of your playoff hopes slowly deflating.

Veton got absolutely fucked sideways this week, limping across the finish line with a pathetic 138 points while Jetmir and Peter's squad flexed 154.3 in his face. That 16-point gap is the kind of deficit you get when you thought streaming defenses was a legitimate strategy, not a cry for help. Veton's roster looked like a fire sale at the clearance bin, and it showed—better luck next week, chief, because this wasn't it.

Faton got absolutely obliterated 118-79.7, a 38-point ass-kicking that made watching his team feel like a war crime. Whatever the fuck he was doing with his lineup this week, it wasn't fantasy football—it was a masterclass in how to completely whiff on every single decision. Ilir didn't even need to break a sweat; Faton's team played like it was auditioning for a minor league team, and it fucking bombed.

matchups.preview: Arben's rolling in at 4-0 like he's a genius when really he's just been carried by narrative beats and bye-week luck—but Rob's coming in winless and absolutely desperate, which means he's either gonna pull off the most embarrassing upset of the season or get absolutely dad-dicked into oblivion with nothing left to lose. Either way, one of these teams is about to remember exactly why they belong where they are.

Flamur's rolling in at 4-0 and about to get absolutely humbled by the reality that his waiver wire luck is about to run out faster than his team's playoff window. Nori's sitting at 3-1 and hungry to prove that last loss was just a speed bump before crushing the undefeated fraud who's been carried by schedule strength and bye-week timing. One of you is about to learn real quick that the regular season doesn't mean shit when the pressure's on.

Both of you are sitting at .500 and about to prove why you belong there—this is a matchup between two managers who've perfected the art of snatching defeat from the jaws of victory. Rinor's probably got three studs on bye while Ben's starting a guy who hasn't been relevant since 2019, so expect maximum chaos and minimum competence. One of you is about to get exposed, and honestly, it could go either way because you're both equally capable of choking.

Adam's barely treading water at 1-3, but congrats on that one win—I'm sure you're real proud of it. Meanwhile Veton's sitting at a perfect 0-4, which is genuinely impressive in how consistently terrible it is. This week one of you finally gets to feel what it's like to not be the biggest dumpster fire in the league, though honestly both your rosters are so mid that the winner's probably just whoever's guy doesn't get injured.

Rilind's 1-3 record speaks louder than any trash talk I could write—dude's basically running a charity at this point, handing wins to everyone else in the league. Faton's sitting pretty at 2-2, which means he's exactly average enough to think he's good but not nearly disciplined enough to actually close out games, making this a perfect matchup between a guy who's already given up and a guy who's about to remember why he shouldn't get cocky.

Jetmir and Peter are about to get a masterclass in how to actually manage a fantasy team from the family member who knows how to win—Ilir's sitting pretty at 3-1 while you two are still trying to figure out what a waiver wire is at 2-2. This Sunday's gonna be the kind of ass-whipping that gets brought up at every family dinner for the next year, and honestly, you deserve it for limping into this matchup like a couple of amateurs. Ilir's coming to remind you why he's the one the family's actually rooting for.
